summary: German chemist Fritz Haber invented the process for making ammonia from air that feeds billions, then kept Germany's WWI war machine supplied and personally led the first large-scale poison gas attack at Ypres in 1915.

evidence.note: born in Breslau, Prussia, now part of Poland
barred from reserve officer rank for being Jewish; long discussion of antisemitism
1904 letter about ammonia traces starts his nitrogen-fixation work
BASF deal and 1909 ammonia breakthrough; Nobel Prize in 1918
decides to develop poison gas and push it on the German high command
gas canisters buried at Ypres and released in April 1915 under his command
Clara's suicide with his service revolver after the Ypres celebration
Nazi-era abandonment, exile and death in 1934
nitrogen runoff, acid rain and ecosystem damage through the present

notes: main_span 1904-1918 covers the ammonia work through WWI gas warfare and the Nobel; exile and death in 1934 are covered more briefly. Zyklon B and the Holocaust get about a minute, so nazism is left out. Host says one gas attack killed 5,000 soldiers; historians give lower figures, but that does not affect any tag.
